fix_commit_message:
fix a memory leak in wasi-nn (#11704)

* fix memory leak

* fix clippy::redundant_field_names

* fix format
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 136500ed555e on top of intro a7e1150019bd via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): The wasi-nn host implementation's compute() function for HostGraphExecutionContext takes ownership of a Vec<NamedTensor> containing Resource<Tensor> handles supplied by the guest. Instead of removing (deleting) these resources from the host-side resource table once they are consumed, the code merely calls Table::get() to borrow/clone the tensor data, leaving the original table entries in place. Since the resource handles are consumed by value and never returned to the guest, the guest has no way to explicitly drop them either, so every call to compute() with input tensors permanently leaks one resource-table slot (and the backend memory referenced by it) per input tensor. Root cause: The refactor of the wasi-nn WIT bindings (commit a7e1150019) rewrote the compute() function to iterate `inputs.iter()` and fetch tensors via `self.table.get(&tensor_resource)` (a non-consuming borrow) rather than removing them from the table, despite the function taking ownership of the `Vec<NamedTensor>` (and thus the associated Resource handles) by value. This created a mismatch between resource ownership semantics (values fully consumed by the call) and the actual table cleanup performed (none), resulting in an unbounded resource-table growth / memory leak for every compute() invocation.
